newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico drug lord's mother may run for election.
newsitem.headline: Mexico drug lord's mother may run for election.

text.p: The mother of Mexico's most wanted drug lord may run for election to congress because she is so popular in her home town, officials of a small, left-wing party said on Thursday.

Aurora Fuentes de Carrillo, mother of fugitive cocaine cartel leader Amado Carrillo Fuentes, has been put forward as a possible candidate in the northwestern state of Sinaloa, Cardenist Party secretary-general Genaro Pineiro told Reuters.
"We have to consider something very important," Pineiro said in a telephone interview.

"The families of people accused of crimes in Mexico have seen their rights trampled on and abused by the authorities -- she could be a way to alert society to the need to fully defend the human rights of criminals' families," Pineiro said.
Carrillo Fuentes, nicknamed "The Lord of the Skies" for his fleet of aircraft smuggling cocaine across Mexico to the United States, is head of the country's top drug cartel.

Pineiro said Aurora Fuentes was one of three "pre-candidates" seeking to run for congress under Cardenist Party colours in Sinaloa in July 6 national elections. A local assembly would decide the nomination next month, he added.
The drug lord's mother may like the political platform of the Cardenist Party, one of Mexico's smallest political groupings.

Pineiro said the party wanted a "serious, deep-seated overhaul of drug policy in Mexico to defend national sovereignty, which has been seriously affected by the instruments which the gringo empire (the United States) has used against us."
The overhaul could consider the "possibility of legalisation" of drugs as a way to attack the trade, he added.

Both Pineiro and party spokesman Eduardo Rivadeneyra said they had not contacted the capo's mother directly. Her name was suggested by locals in her home town of Navolato, 600 miles (1,000 km) northwest of Mexico City, they added.

"Mrs. Carrillo, independent of the behaviour of her children, is a popular leader who is strong among the co-operative farmers of her town and that's why she is being invited to stand," Rivadeneyra said.

A 52-year-old widow and mother of 12, Aurora Fuentes de Carrillo last hit the headlines in January. That was when a joint police and army squad swooped down on a lavish wedding party at the family ranch. The drug lord's sister Aurora was getting married and Amado Carrillo himself was invited.
A timely tip-off allowed the "Lord of the Skies" to escape his pursuers. Last week the Mexican government said the leak came from the country's top anti-drug warrior, Gen. Jesus Gutierrez Rebollo.
Rebollo is now in jail, charged with taking bribes from Carrillo Fuentes in exchange for protecting the cartel.
